title: Tests You Can Trust
description: Write and commission tests that would actually fail if the code were wrong — specifying behaviour instead of accepting whatever a generated suite hands back, and proving each test can catch the bug it claims to catch.

title: Review Workflow and PR Craft
description: Put an AI-assisted change in front of another human in a form they can actually review — a description that gives a cold reader real context, a diff split into pieces someone can hold in their head, honest disclosure of what was generated, and the skill of responding to review on code you didn't personally write.

title: CI, Builds and Reproducibility
description: Make the build fail on your own machine before it fails on someone else's — pinning what your project depends on, reading a CI failure that never happened locally, understanding what flaky tests actually cost, and choosing the checks that genuinely belong before merge.

title: Deploy, Rollback and Migrations
description: Ship a change you can undo — including the ones that touch stored data. Schema migrations that stay safe while the old code is still running, generated migrations that quietly destroy something someone still reads, feature flags that separate deploying from releasing, and the specific discipline of staying compatible with yourself across a rolling deploy.

title: Observability and On-Call Reality
description: Instrument a change so that when it misbehaves in production you can find out why — structured logs that answer the question a 3am reader actually has, metrics that surface a problem before a user files a ticket, alerts worth waking someone for, and the specific discipline of debugging generated code you last read a month ago.
